thread:
sasha: Heads up — about a dozen EU users hit 403 on /analytics right after SSO. They appear provisioned but their role is 'basic' instead of 'analytics_viewer'.

matt: Any logs or example users?

sasha: Example: carla@company.eu. From the app audit we see provisioning happened but role string was truncated. Pasted redacted SAML assertion snippet below:
```xml
<saml:Attribute Name="roles">analytics_viewer;team:analytics;source:okta</saml:Attribute>
```
But in our provisioning log it shows `roles=analytics_vie` (missing last chars).

security-eng: That smells like an attribute-length/transform issue during mapping. I reproduced locally: if Accept-Language header is set (e.g., `fr-FR`) and the attribute payload crosses a certain byte boundary, Okta mapping layer truncates at 64 bytes in our tenant config. Our JIT expects the full semicolon-delimited list and does `split(';')[0]` — so truncation yields a non-matching role id.

matt: Can you paste the Okta mapping expression you're seeing?

security-eng: In the Okta inline transform we currently have something like:
```javascript
var r = user.profile.roles;
return r ? r.split(';')[0] : null;
```
But there's also a custom transform upstream doing `profile.roles = profile.roles.substring(0,64)` for legacy reasons when `locale` is set. That substring is the culprit.

okta-platform: Confirmed on our side — for the assertion sent to SP we logged `attributeValue` length 13 for that attribute and an `attributeTruncated=true` flag. We also show Accept-Language present for those requests.

oncall: Temporary mitigation — I'm going to add a canary mapping: domain `@company.eu` -> `analytics_viewer` for the analytics app until we deploy a proper fix. Creating an ACL rule now and will scope to 12 users.

devops-bot: deploy started for canary rule (deploy id: #6789). Rolling to 2 instances.

alice: For the long-term fix we need better auditability: when JIT provisioning runs, record an `assertion_sha256` and include the Okta `requestId` (or `attributeTruncated` flag) in the audit event. Also record the KMS key alias used for signing/verification of the provisioning payload so we can trace back. Can we add those to provisioning logs?

security-eng: Agreed. Action items: 1) Remove legacy `substring(0,64)` transform in Okta mapping and replace with safe parsing that prefers group membership if role parse fails. 2) Add `assertion_sha256` and `okta.requestId` to provisioning audit events. 3) Update RBAC fallback order: assertion.role -> groups claim -> email domain mapping -> default.

matt: I'll open the infra ticket and PR template. Assigning to @security-eng and @devops for the Okta mapping and rollout runbook. Ticket SE-9483 created with logs attached.

sasha: Canary mitigation is live and affected users report access restored. Will monitor for 24h.

alice: Also add a short runbook entry to the SSO incident runbook: how to detect attribute truncation (look for `attributeTruncated=true` in Okta logs and `role` length < expected) and the temporary domain fallback step.

security-eng: PR for mapping changes opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4125. Need infra approvals for Okta tenant change; target permanent patch by Friday EOD.

matt: Thanks all. Postmortem / follow-up: include timeline, root cause (legacy substring transform + Accept-Language interaction), and the audit logging change.

sasha: Closing thread when we see 24h stable. :white_check_mark:
